💵 Brent near $114 as attacks on Saudi energy sites sustain risk premium
Brent crude traded around $113.75 a barrel on Friday, on track for a third consecutive weekly gain, after Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure kept a geopolitical risk premium firmly in place.
👉 The attacks have targeted key Saudi sites in recent days, including King Fahd International Airport in Dammam and the Shaybah oilfield, with the Gulf Cooperation Council reporting casualties and material damage. Houthi forces also claimed strikes on Riyadh's Defense Ministry, [Aramco's Yanbu facility and Abha airport](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76611). 
Analysts say the market is pricing in the risk of further disruption to Middle Eastern energy flows, with attention also on the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb.

✡️ Netanyahu moves to lock down West Bank days before Israeli election
Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered the immediate closure of Hebron and preparations for a full lockdown across the West Bank.
🔊“I have instructed the IDF and the security forces to immediately impose a closure on the city of Hebron and to prepare for a full lockdown across all of Judea and Samaria starting today,” the Israeli PM wrote on X after a security assessment with senior defense and intelligence officials.
He said Israeli forces were stepping up operations and carrying out mass arrests, vowing to pursue Hamas members “everywhere and at all times.”
The move follows a shooting early in the morning at the northern entrance to Hebron. Two Palestinians were reported killed, while six Israeli soldiers were injured.
Netanyahu also ordered his Likud party to cancel all political events following the attack, the party said.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
🇮🇱 Israel providing intel to Saudi Arabia for Yemen strikes – reports
The IDF has provided Riyadh with “exceptional” intelligence “capabilities to assist its military operations against the Houthis,” an anonymous defense official told JPost.
👉 The intel-sharing, provided via “US mediation,” lines up “with Israel’s national interests and directives from the political leadership,” the official said.
Israel benefits from the exchange “because it wears down the military strength of an Israeli enemy that is preparing and planning to harm us in the future,” and “learning a great deal” about the situation on the ground, observing “methods of operations and tactics,” and weapons types used.
➡️ The intel support comes against the background of reports that the IDF is on “heighted alert” for some kind of [potential Houthi ground or sea assault inside Israel itself.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76195)
It also follows reports that Benjamin Netanyahu had proposed joining the military campaign against Ansar Allah, but was shot down by MBS, who declined over fears of the domestic and regional repercussions of being seen as collaborating with Israel, whose treatment of the Palestinians Riyadh has formally condemned.
Ansar Allah has consistently accused the House of Saud and other regional monarchies of being “puppets,” “mercenaries” and “servants” of the US and Israel.
The Houthi-aligned Yemeni military reported Thursday that Saudi air and missile strikes had targeted Yemen 2.9k+ times since July’s resumption of hostilities. JPost’s source did not clarify when Israel began sharing intel, or what percentage of overall Saudi attacks have been based on info provided by the IDF.
